candidate: New opt-in Go action selector around unchanged DK7 selected-outcome counter memory, no mutation of DK7 or original R8

policy.observation: Only original public image 7x7x3, direction 0..3 and exact DoorKey mission; feature definition remains original dk7.Context
policy.preference: When original learned positive-reward chooser has admissible evidence, keep its chosen native action. Otherwise propose one of 0..6 with the fewest *native observed* samples for the public context; tie break deterministically by a hash of the public context and mutable native count vector. No hidden state, hardcoded DoorKey task solution, external action selection, arbitrary environment metadata, or reward injection.
policy.update: Reuse unchanged original DK7 transactional Commit/Feedback and ObserveFit, only one selected real submitted action can change sample memory.
policy.capacity: Inherit unchanged DK7 4096 samples, 512 contexts, 150000-byte snapshot; no extra learnable memory.
policy.checkpoint: Use original DK7 native content-addressed snapshot, cold restore, identical next native selected action for identical public context and observation counts.
policy.negative_controls: Reject malformed public mission/shape, pending action re-proposal, wrong selected-action feedback, tampered checkpoint and no unselected feedback.
policy.alternative: Original unchanged DK7 reward-gated abstention; external public-only collector separately labelled; uniform-action exploration at matched budgets. These are *future* paired MG04 controls, not implicit proof from focused source tests.

qualification.allowed: Focused native Go unit tests on Linux and Windows; source-exact identity of unchanged DK7/R8 sources; no original-world live DoorKey evaluation in this gate
required: Before new evidence: frozen prereg checksum and parent/source identity
At previously unseen public context, propose a real legal 0..6 native action rather than abstain
After real selected feedback, next action responds to observed action-support counts
Original DK7 positive reward action takes precedence over novel uncertainty proposal
Cold snapshot-and-restore yields identical native proposed action
Two-host focused tests are green, no skipped tests
